title: Today in one sentence
text: Before the open on Wednesday, the numbers are still Tuesday's closing prices, so the thing to watch is whether the market keeps leaning toward health stocks and away from big tech, with Lockheed Martin's report coming Thursday morning and the Fed meeting on October 27 and 28.

title: Lockheed Martin reports on Thursday
text: Lockheed Martin said it will share its third quarter results before the market opens on Thursday, October 22, with a call at 8:30 a.m. Eastern. Its stock closed Tuesday at $548.71, a little under the $554 low end of analyst price targets. Reports can move a stock in either direction, so Thursday is a good day to watch.

title: Bond yields are the quiet worry
text: The 10 year Treasury yield averaged 4.99% in September, up from 4.06% a year earlier, and news reports put it near 5.1% in mid October. A yield is the interest the government pays for a loan. When it rises, safer bonds become more tempting and stocks can feel pressure.

title: Chip stocks swing a lot
text: AMD closed at $534.74. Over the past year it has traded between $188.22 and $658.52, which is a very wide range. Nvidia has a smaller range, $164.27 to $243.37. A wide range is a sign that the price can move a lot in both directions.

title: Lesson 16: What is volatility?
text: Volatility is how much a price jumps around. A calm stock moves a little each day, like a bike on a flat road. A volatile stock goes up and down a lot, like a bike on a hilly trail. You can see it in the 52 week range: AMD traded between about $188 and $659 in a year, while the Schwab dividend fund SCHD stayed between about $26 and $35. Volatility is not good or bad by itself. It just tells you how bumpy the ride might be, and it is why people who need their money soon often like calmer investments. This is for learning, not advice to buy or sell anything.
